threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'the Loo' for the toilet instead of 'loo,' and suddenly everyone’s side-eyeing you like a tourist.
Caught the 59 last night—two blokes arguing about which chicken shop was better. It was like a live review show on wheels. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing a spontaneous concert in the courtyard while kids play hopscotch on the sidewalk. That's when Neukölln felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you have a spontaneous dance-off in the middle of a street market while nearby cafés keep serving coffee. It's pure Berlin magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they maneuver through a BART delay. Tourists just stare at their phones; locals weave through the chaos like pros.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo hop off the 21 with a bouquet, casually dodging a pigeon fight. Only in SF do formal and chaotic collide like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals flock to Park Güell, but half the time, we’re at the plaça just chatting over a drink, keeping it low-key.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them awkwardly holding the metro map upside down, trying to navigate the labyrinthine L2 line on a Monday morning.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid eye contact with the buskers on Kingsland Road, like they’re a wild animal you’re scared of.
Heard a bloke on the 12 bus at 2 AM arguing with a pigeon over a chip. The bird was winning. Peckham nightlife really is something else.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street performer juggling flaming torches next to a baby stroller on Karl-Marx-Straße. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab place that stays open all night, serving fresh döner to the club crowds while the U-Bahn is on strike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're from here when they react to the BART delays with a resigned shrug instead of panic. It’s the city’s soundtrack.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just watched a guy serenade a sleeping bus rider with a ukulele at Civic Center. Classic Muni moment—only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think La Rambla is the heart of Barcelona, but Gràcia’s narrow streets and local festes are where the real pulse of the city beats.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with their T-10 card, staring at the machines like they owe them money.
